page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, the processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports x86_64 architecture instructions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16 extensions) and AES cryptography. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfr7.2xlarge in the average tier across most compute and memory metrics. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1320.0 and a multi-core score of 5074.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 9658.56. Memory bandwidth tests show 465.34 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 51.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations perform reliably, with Redis SET operations reaching 7.99 million operations per second. However, the instance exhibits performance limitations on larger workloads; while it processes a small 135M LLM model efficiently, its performance on a medium 7B LLM model is weak, generating only 6.39 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfr7.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention. This hardware configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, including medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, in-memory data processing, and static web serving. It is less suitable for heavy parallel computing, large-scale machine learning inference, or storage-heavy applications due to the lack of local disks and moderate network throughput.
